metadata.title: GetMSIInformation
metadata.description:
The script creates a WPF-based GUI that allows users to drag and drop MSI files to view their properties such as Product Name, Manufacturer, Product Version, Product Code, and Upgrade Code.
It also provides functionality to copy these properties to the clipboard and to clear the displayed information.
Additionally, the script includes options to install and uninstall a context menu item for MSI files to retrieve their properties.

findings.title: Dynamic PowerShell code execution
findings.description: Dynamic evaluation can make a script harder to inspect and may enable downloaded or constructed code to run.

findings.title: Network retrieval combined with code execution
findings.description: The same file contains both a network retrieval pattern and a dynamic execution pattern. This combination merits review and is not by itself proof of malicious intent.

evidence.snippet: Start-Process -FilePath $Script:PowerShellPath -ArgumentList "-NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -WindowStyle Minimized -Command `"Invoke-Expression (Invoke-RestMethod 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MichaelEscamilla/GetMSIInformation/main/GetMSIInformation.ps1')`""  …  Start-Process -FilePath $Script:PowerShellPath -ArgumentList "-NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -WindowStyle Minimized -File `"$PSCommandPath`" -FilePath `"$FilePath`""

findings.title: Encoded or compressed content used with dynamic execution
findings.description: Encoded or compressed data is used alongside dynamic evaluation. This can appear in legitimate tooling; review the surrounding logic.
